Not recorded as ADRs, because they follow from the decisions above: the audit chain (change records,
monthly reconciliation, drift detection; framework layer 7), the rollout plan
([`../03-rollout-plan.md`](../03-rollout-plan.md)) and the CI-agent setup
(layer 5; covered in parts by ADR-0006 and ADR-0007).

Rule: an accepted ADR is not edited. A changed decision gets a new ADR that supersedes the old one.

## Refinements since acceptance

Writing and testing the files in [`../../examples/`](../../examples/README.md) made some details more
precise. None changes a decision, so no ADR is superseded; the framework carries the current wording.

- **ADR-0003:** "merge approval = deploy approval" gains two conditions: squash-only merges (OD16)
  and deploying only the current tip of `main`, because a writer can re-run an old deploy run for
  30 days and roll prod back without approval (OD17; examples finding 4).
- **ADR-0004:** "the approver sees the prod diff" means the approver sees **which** prod resources and
  properties change, not the new values, which stay out of the job summary so that secrets stay out of
  logs; values are reviewed in the code of the stopped PR. The approval is also bound to git history
  (examples E7, finding 2), and an early approval can match a later change outside the stack, an
  accepted gap until G19 (OD18).
- **ADR-0007:** the "read-only allowlist" became two exact repo scripts, because Claude Code already runs
  read-only commands without a prompt and wildcard rules can write files (examples finding 19); phase 1
  adds a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule and `autoMode.classifyAllShell` (OD21). `sandbox.excludedCommands`
  entries need a trailing ` *` and are paired with `ask` rules, so each excluded CLI call prompts, auto
  mode included (examples finding 22).

After the independent review (`work/07-review.md`; owner decisions from OD22, 2026-11-09). Two
changes are decisions and got their own ADR: ADR-0011 (database changes) and ADR-0012, which
supersedes parts of ADR-0003 and ADR-0010. The others narrow how a decision is carried out:

- **ADR-0002:** "nobody holds standing prod write" now also covers who administers Identity Center:
  permission sets and assignments are code owned by the L3 owner team only, other changes raise an
  alert, `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` is denied in the prod OU and member-account root
  credentials are removed (OD23). The management account stays outside SCPs: detected, not prevented.
- **ADR-0003 / ADR-0004:** what runs in the deploy job is limited from phase 1: one GitHub
  environment per kind of stack (`production-iam` for the IAM stack), bounded domain deploy roles,
  no install scripts except a reviewed allowlist, and an agent review on infrastructure PRs (OD22).
  This was OD20's phase-2 roadmap item. The risk stop's scope is unchanged (OD15).
- **ADR-0008:** the k0s exception gets conditions: a separate `production-k0s` environment (was
  optional), a namespaced, time-limited ServiceAccount token instead of a kubeconfig, and the
  Kubernetes API audit log; target is k0s trusting GitHub OIDC directly (OD24).
- **ADR-0006:** its example entry `serverCommand` = `["npx", "<package>@<exact-version>"]` is no longer allowed: it pins the package, not its dependencies. "Pinned catalogue" now covers what reaches every laptop: the marketplace is pinned
  to a protected release tag, every plugin (internal ones too) to a commit, auto-update is off, and
  local MCP servers are admitted only as immutable artifacts (OD26).
- **ADR-0003 / ADR-0007:** managed deny rules for `gh pr review` and the `gh` token file from phase 1,
  as hygiene behind OD5; a login register maps GitHub accounts to people (OD25). The parts of
  ADR-0003 that ADR-0012 supersedes are listed in ADR-0012.
- **ADR-0009:** log groups the agent may read get a second layer outside application code: a
  CloudWatch Logs masking policy with custom identifiers, no `logs:Unmask` for agent-usable roles,
  and a SAST rule against logging whole events (OD28).
- **ADR-0005:** JIT requests and approvals are Linear issues from a template, mirrored to the
  evidence bucket with Object Lock; no longer "a channel" left open (OD30).
=== 0001-prod-changes-only-through-ci.md
## 3. Decision

"A + D2'": option A is the default path for every production change, incidents included. A narrow JIT
fallback exists only when the PR path cannot be used during an incident (ADR-0005). The owner accepts
that this fallback meets the approval rule only partly (Options §9 Q2). Incident target: ≤ 30 min from
decision to apply.

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** the PR, its approvals, the run log and CloudTrail form one evidence chain keyed by
  commit SHA. Agent-written and human-written changes pass the same checks (S10).
- **Negative / trade-offs:** slower incident fixes; operations that are not in IaC must first be
  written as code or a runbook. Two write paths remain (PR and JIT), while the framing asked for one.
- **Risks & how we watch them:** the fallback stays narrow only if most incidents are expressible in
  IaC (unknown, Options §8). Metrics: JIT grants per month, share of incidents needing non-IaC
  operations; above about 25 % (⚠️ starting threshold), make the PR lane faster or add a runbook, never widen JIT.
- **Example:** Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m. The responder's agent proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s in
  `serverless.yml`; the PR is labelled `incident`; the on-call approver reviews and approves; CI
  packages, previews prod and deploys with the OIDC role. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6).
- **Next steps:** measure the incident PR lane on one service first (phase 1).

## 5. References
=== 0002-no-standing-prod-write-read-only-agent-identity.md
## 3. Decision

Option B. Prod is written only by the CI pipeline role, or by an approved, time-boxed JIT grant
(ADR-0005). The standing prod role is `ProdReadMetadata` [design name]: metrics, redacted log groups,
configuration of services whose secrets are resolved at runtime; no data-plane reads of claim stores;
1-hour role session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). From phase 2, SCPs on the prod OU deny data-plane reads and
direct Lambda updates except for named roles (pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4, R4.6 #3). Option C follows in phase 3.

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** once standing write and broad read roles are removed (end of phase 1), an agent,
  even a manipulated one, cannot write prod AWS or read AWS claim stores with the engineer's standing
  identity (data-plane action list ⚠️ G13); k0s and GCP follow the same principle, mechanisms open
  (G1, G3). In non-prod the agent keeps broad rights (`NonProdDeveloper`, ADR-0010 L1). Compliance gets least privilege enforced by IAM (S1).
- **Negative / trade-offs:** during the transition, engineers lose raw logs and configuration of
  services not yet redacted. Configuration values then come from the IaC code; raw logs need a
  data-read grant in an incident. Process rules remain where
  IAM cannot separate engineer and agent: no agent in the JIT terminal (D2).
- **Risks & how we watch them:** SSO-token theft during a session could open later grants (⚠️);
  mitigations [design] are a short portal session and a fresh sign-in before a grant. The data-plane action
  list is incomplete (⚠️ G13). Identity Center assignment export is reviewed quarterly.
- **Next steps:** phase 1 removes broad read roles only after the minimal real-data read flow works,
  then removes standing prod write once its prerequisites are in place.

## 5. References
=== 0004-risk-stop-on-risky-prod-diffs.md
## 3. Decision

Option C [design]. The deploy job on `main` previews prod. On stateful replace/delete, an IAM
change, a network or security-group change, or (from phase 2) an advisory policy finding, it stops
and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a PR (the workflow does not, as "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
approve pull requests" stays off, 📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3) adding
`deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` with the SHA and preview hash (owned by the stack's owners and the
on-call group, OD8, OD9); the first approver approves it
(OD13). If that approver is unavailable, another stack owner approves; this makes three people and
is recorded as a deviation (OD11). After the merge the workflow previews again on the new HEAD and
continues only if the hash matches. Serverless uses `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI because
differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2). A `mandatory` Pulumi policy violation always
blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2; policy packs from phase 2).

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** the person who approves now sees the prod diff for the changes that can do lasting
  damage. Still two people in the normal case.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** while a stack is stopped, later deploys to it stop too (the hash
  differs), including an incident fix, until the approval lands or the change is reverted. One more review round when the stop fires.
- **Risks & how we watch them:** preview output may not be stable enough to hash (⚠️ Options §8); if
  not, compare a structured summary. Until phase 2, the risk stop is the only compensation for OD8;
  Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and policy packs follow. k0s and Firebase have no
  preview step in this design (⚠️ G1, G2).
- **Next steps:** risk stop in the deploy job in phase 1.

## 5. References
=== 0005-break-glass-is-time-limited-jit.md
## 3. Decision

Option C [design], used only during an incident when the PR path cannot be used.

- **Request:** command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub.
- **Approval:** the on-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant; the on-call approver counts as
  owner of the service (OD13).
- **Grant:** `InfraOperator-<service>` [design name], assigned via `CreateAccountAssignment` and removed
  via `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2); role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4).
- **Execution:** the incident responder types the commands in a terminal without an agent (D2, OD7).
- **Example request** (illustrative command ⚠️): "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage.
  Run `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
- **After:** CloudTrail writes in the window are compared with the list; a codify PR follows by a
  fixed deadline; drift detection runs until it merges.

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** no standing prod write even for emergencies; every use has an approval, a window and
  a reconciliation.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** meets the approval rule only partly (owner accepted). "No agent in the
  JIT terminal" is a process rule: the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
- **Risks & how we watch them:** deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions, so a grant
  can run up to about 2 h (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which keeps
  the user blocked ≥ 12 h (📖 R2.4.4); no night-time path to apply it is designed yet (⚠️ G20).
  Metrics: JIT used where a PR was possible, writes outside the list, late codify PRs (review at 1).
- **Next steps:** minimal JIT with per-grant CloudTrail comparison and a manual drift check of the
  touched stacks in phase 1 (a temporary deviation from D2); revocation SCP and
  automated reconciliation in phase 2.

## 5. References
=== 0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md
## 3. Decision

Option C. The catalogue is a file in git, changed by PR under the L3 owner team.

- **Plugins:** only Papaya's marketplace via managed `strictKnownMarketplaces`, plus
  `blockedMarketplaces` (📖 R1.4.2); sources pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only);
  `disableSideloadFlags` (📖 R1.4.2); version floor covering the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
- **MCP:** `allowedMcpServers` with `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4); match by
  `serverUrl` or `serverCommand` (exact argv), never `serverName`, which "is not a security control"
  (📖 R1.3.3); `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7).
- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher, local or remote, what it reads and where it sends data,
  supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status, no token passthrough (📖 R6.4.2), pinned version.
  Example entry: `serverCommand` = `["npx", "<package>@<exact-version>"]` [design; placeholder].
- **CI:** server-managed settings do not reach a CI job (📖 R1.7.10); CI uses a managed-settings
  file on the runner and a fixed MCP set, because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
  (📖 R1.3.5).

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier records (P4c); unknown servers are
  refused before they load.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** waiting time for new tools; review effort for 1–2 DevSecOps people.
- **Risks & how we watch them:** the enforced copy lives in server-managed settings, edited in the
  admin console by Owners, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports and diffs it with git monthly until
  G18 is solved (ADR-0007). `disableSideloadFlags` does not cover `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add`
  (📖 R1.4.2), so the MCP allowlist must be locked. No per-group targeting in server-managed settings
  (📖 R1.1.6). Tool description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️). Without MDM, laptops can
  bypass server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11). Evidence: OTel `plugin_installed` /
  `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6).
- **Next steps:** catalogue v1 in phase 1 (may slip to phase 2 only with owner agreement).

## 5. References
=== 0007-agent-settings-are-hygiene-not-the-boundary.md
## 3. Decision

Option B. The boundary is IAM (ADR-0002) and the merge gate (ADR-0003). Managed settings set safe,
uniform defaults:

- `permissions.defaultMode` = `"default"` (Manual), with a read-only allowlist that excludes `aws`, `pulumi`,
  `serverless` (D1, OD7b; 📖 R6.9.3); auto mode stays available and is measured.
- `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` (📖 R1.2.2); `requiredMinimumVersion` floor (📖 R1.1.13).
- Sandbox with `~/.aws` hidden (📖 R1.6.3, R1.6.4) [design]; `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` in
  `sandbox.excludedCommands` [design]; `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` kept `true` (OD12, 📖 R5.5.5b).
- OTel exporter without prompt content (📖 R1.1.20, R5.5.4).

Outside managed settings: the `--restricted` flag (📖 R6.9.1b) in CI, set in the workflow file under
CODEOWNERS, and, as a process rule, in the incident-analysis session; a setting cannot force it
(📖 R6.9.1) (D3).

Phase 1 ships `defaultMode`, the allowlist, bypass removal, the catalogue keys, the version floor and
OTel; the rest of the baseline follows in phase 2 (OD4).

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** a bypassed or misconfigured agent still cannot write prod or read AWS PHI
  stores with the engineer's standing identity, once standing write is removed (PHI paths outside IAM
  are process-only, ADR-0009). Compliance gets
  one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** more prompts than auto mode; a prompt for every `aws` read. S5
  ("nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed") is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
- **Risks & how we watch them:** the auto-mode classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions
  (📖 R6.3.5); fallback to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers it (D1). The live
  settings are edited in the admin console, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports them monthly and
  diffs them with git until a better method exists (G18).
  Until phase 2 there is no sandbox: `~/.aws` is readable and the network open; in auto mode the
  classifier is the only gate. `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` run outside the sandbox even later
  (📖 R1.6.4; ⚠️ inference): repo code that the agent can edit (Pulumi programs, Serverless
  plugins) then runs with network and `~/.aws`, and SSO-token theft remains possible; bounded by
  ADR-0002. With OD12, Manual mode does not mean a prompt for every command (📖 R5.5.5b).
- **Next steps:** phase-1 subset; planted-injection test in phase 3.

## 5. References
=== 0008-oidc-no-long-lived-ci-keys.md
## 3. Decision

Option C.

- **AWS:** GitHub OIDC (📖 R3.4.1); the prod role trusts only the `production` environment of the
  monorepo (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4), ideally narrowed by `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
- **GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization (📖 R3.4.5b).
- **k0s/Firebase exception** (OD1, OD6): CI deploy credentials only, until it is checked whether they
  can use OIDC. Conditions [design]: a `production` environment secret, never a repository secret
  (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3); GitHub-hosted runners, because on self-hosted runners environment secrets act
  like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5); if k0s needs a self-hosted runner, it is dedicated to the
  `production` deploy and the residual risk is recorded (⚠️ G15); a single source of truth; owner, expiry, rotation.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` default "restricted" (📖 R3.5.3); actions pinned by lockfile or full SHA (📖 R3.5.5).

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** no stored AWS or GCP keys to leak (S2); every deploy credential is tied to a reviewed
  workflow on `main`.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** one-time migration; slower action updates. The exception remains until
  G1/G2 are solved.
- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can change or delete the environment, and a deleted
  environment comes back without protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); alerts and a settings comparison cover it.
  The GitHub Apps used for CI agents and the required check have their own keys (⚠️ G19).
  Runtime credentials inside the cluster are out of the exception (OD6).
- **Next steps:** OIDC and removal of stored keys in phase 1; k0s/Firebase credentials moved to
  environment secrets before standing prod write is removed.

## 5. References
=== 0009-agent-stays-outside-phi.md
## 3. Decision

Option C.

- **PHI:** never in an agent session. A human reads in a terminal without an agent and gives the
  agent a redacted summary. A store that holds PHI counts as PHI unless the agent reads a view without
  it [design].
- **Other personal data:** readable within an approved request naming one tenant, purpose, store,
  window and agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9); approved by an approver ≠ requester and
  co-approved by the tenant's data owner [design]; data-read role, 1 h [design]. The same request
  applies when a human reads PHI. At night the
  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day [design].
- **Partner documents:** reproduced with synthetic documents or de-identified first [design].
- **Non-prod:** synthetic or masked only (GĐ-14); no prod copies (S11).

This is a target, not a guarantee: "no agent in the PHI terminal" is a process rule [design] with
the same weakness as D2, since the grant is reachable from the same laptop.

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2); one record per
  exception (S9). Assumes injection succeeds and limits what it can reach.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** debugging with redacted or synthetic data; a request for each real read.
- **Risks & how we watch them:** of the 17 paths to PHI (research 1.11.4), tickets, chat, pasted text,
  admin pages, CI logs, prod AI traces and fixtures are covered by process only; k0s and GCP stores follow the same principle
  with mechanisms still open (G1, G3). Per-tenant scoping through session tags (📖 R2.1.8) is
  unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️). During a data-read window a stolen SSO
  token could open the grant (⚠️, ADR-0007). Data-plane deny actions are incomplete (⚠️ G13). Planted-injection test in
  phase 3.
- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and the minimal real-data read flow in phase 1; data-plane SCP in
  phase 2.

152	   152	## Limits of the risk stop
153	   153	
154	   154	The risk stop answers one framework problem: on GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before
155	   155	apply (framework §1). It catches **risky prod diffs that nobody looked at**. It is not a boundary
156	   156	against **malicious or prompt-injected code that was approved**:
157	   157	
158	   158	- The stack's own code runs with the stack's prod deploy role: `npm` packages are installed before the
159	   159	  credentials, with install scripts off (OD22), but the Pulumi program runs during `preview` and

159	   159	  credentials, with install scripts off (OD22), but the Pulumi program runs during `preview` and
160	   160	  `up`, and Serverless plugins during `package`/`diff`/`deploy`. That code could call AWS
161	   161	  directly, or tamper with files the classifier reads, in the same job. The defence against it
162	   162	  is the PR review itself, and from phase 2 IAM Access Analyzer and policy packs (layer 5).
163	   163	- A stronger variant [design, not in the framework]: preview with a separate prod **preview**
164	   164	  role (read and state access, no write), run the classifier in its own job on a fresh
165	   165	  checkout without credentials, and assume the deploy role only in a later job after the stop.
166	   166	  It adds a role and a job split; it is an open question for the owner.
167	   167	- `pulumi up` previews again before applying. A change made outside the pipeline between the
168	   168	  two previews (JIT, drift) is not re-checked. `pulumi preview --save-plan` + `pulumi up --plan`
169	   169	  would bind the two, but update plans are experimental (📖 R4.1.3).
170	   170	- Concurrency: a running deploy is never cancelled, but GitHub cancels a run that is still
171	   171	  pending when a newer one arrives for the same group (📖 GitHub docs source,
172	   172	  `data/reusables/actions/actions-group-concurrency.md`). Some merged commits therefore have no
173	   173	  deploy run of their own; the newer run deploys them too, and the change record must link both
174	   174	  commits to that run. `queue: max` would give every commit its own run, but the same page says
175	   175	  the order "is not guaranteed": an older commit could then deploy after a newer one and undo it
176	   176	  in prod. So the default is kept on purpose [design].
177	   177	- The type lists are examples. For types that are missing, the rule on property names
178	   178	  (`policy`, `role`, `securityGroup`, `vpcConfig`, `public`, `authorization`, `logging`, …;
179	   179	  a narrower set on creates) catches some changes, not all.
180	   180	- **Code in the deploy job can act as either deploy role of its environment.** `id-token: write`
181	   181	  is job-wide, so the Pulumi program, Serverless plugins and any allowlisted install script can
182	   182	  request the job's OIDC token (⚠️ from memory of GitHub's OIDC docs) and assume either role that
183	   183	  trusts that environment. Since OD22 (phase 1) that is a domain stack's bounded roles, never the
184	   184	  IAM stack's role (`production-iam`, E4), and no other install script runs
185	   185	  (`npm_config_ignore_scripts`). Still on the phase-2 roadmap with OD15: a separate preview role
186	   186	  and a build job without `id-token`.
187	   187	- **Open gap:** nothing proves that a deploy really stopped at `stopped_commit` with the
188	   188	  approved hash. An approval merged early (naming a commit whose deploy did not stop, with a
189	   189	  hash computed in advance, which needs knowledge of prod inputs) is accepted if a later change
190	   190	  **outside** the stack's directory, such as a shared library, produces exactly that diff. Changes
191	   191	  inside the stack's directory are rejected. Watching the whole repository instead would cancel
192	   192	  every approval at each unrelated merge in a monorepo. The fix is for the approval-gate app to
193	   193	  check, on the approval PR, that the stopped run's summary carries the same hash (G19) [design].
194	   194	  `test_known_gap_early_approval_and_change_outside_the_stack` documents the current behaviour.
195	   195	- The approver of the approval PR sees **which** prod resources and properties change, not the
196	   196	  new values (the summary never prints values, to keep secrets out of logs). The values are
197	   197	  reviewed in the code of the stopped PR. Framework layer 3 and ADR-0004 say the approver "sees
198	   198	  the prod diff"; that wording is too strong and is corrected in the framework's final pass.
199	   199	- Any commit to the stack's directory between the stop and the approval merge cancels the
200	   200	  approval: the author names the newer stopped commit and the owner approves again. In an
201	   201	  incident that is one more review round.
202	   202	- `npm ci` runs before the credentials with lifecycle scripts off (OD22). The allowlisted
203	   203	  packages' scripts still run, and could write to `$GITHUB_ENV` / `$GITHUB_PATH` and so influence
204	   204	  later steps that hold credentials; that is why the allowlist is an L3 path.
205	   205	- If the newest merge to `main` carries `[skip ci]` (or similar) in its message, no push run
206	   206	  exists for the tip and the older runs refuse to deploy; prod stays behind until the next merge
207	   207	  (📖 GitHub docs source, `content/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/skip-workflow-runs.md`,
208	   208	  via review). Operator action: merge an empty change.
209	   209	- Within 7 days, an approved change that is reverted and then merged again with identical code
210	   210	  passes without a new approval. This is intended: it is the same code and the same prod diff
211	   211	  that an owner approved.
212	   212	- The binding relies on squash-only merges (`ruleset-main.json`); with merge commits, a PR's
213	   213	  inner commits would be invisible to the first-parent check.

216	   216	
217	   217	Points the framework text does not yet say; carried into the framework in the final pass.
218	   218	Owner decisions 2026-11-09 (framework OD14–OD18): findings 1, 3 and 4 accepted; the risk stop keeps
219	   219	its current scope (OD15); the early-approval gap is an accepted limit for G19 to close (OD18).
220	   220	Step 2: finding 16 accepted (OD19); the job-wide OIDC token limit goes to the phase-2 roadmap

222	   222	into phase 1.
223	   223	
224	   224	1. **The risk-stop classifier must be an L3 path** [design]. The deploy runs it from the merged
225	   225	   commit, so a PR that edits it together with an IAM change, approved by the domain team, could
226	   226	   switch the stop off. `CODEOWNERS` adds `/tools/risk-stop/` to the L3 owner team. Confirmed by
227	   227	   the owner (OD14): it extends the canonical L3 list of framework layer 5.
228	   228	2. **An approval must be bound to git history, not only to a hash** [design]. Two review rounds
229	   229	   found ways for one PR to carry its own risky change and approval, or for an approval to be
230	   230	   reused. Rules now: read from git objects only; file named `<stopped_commit>.yaml`, never
231	   231	   edited; stopped commit and approval commit both on `main`'s first-parent history, in that
232	   232	   order; the approval commit touches only `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`; the stack's directory
233	   233	   and the classifier unchanged since the stopped commit; at most 7 days old.
234	   234	3. **Squash-only merges** [design]: `ruleset-main.json` allows only squash, so each PR is one
235	   235	   commit on `main`. Cost: PR-internal history is not kept on `main`.
236	   236	4. **Deploy only the tip of `main`** [design]: people with write access can re-run a workflow run
237	   237	   for up to 30 days, with the same `GITHUB_SHA` (📖 GitHub docs source,
238	   238	   `content/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs.md`, via review). An
239	   239	   old deploy run re-run would roll prod back without any approval. `deploy-prod.yml` stops unless
240	   240	   the run's commit is the current tip of `main`, read with `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/heads/main`
241	   241	   (✅ branch-only form; `commits/main` could resolve to a tag named `main`). This is a new
242	   242	   condition for framework layer 3's "merge approval = deploy approval" list.
243	   243	5. **Classification beyond the framework's categories** [design]: the property-name rule, the
244	   244	   audit/detection category and "an unknown operation stops" go beyond layer 3's list
245	   245	   (stateful replace/delete, IAM, network, policy finding).
246	   246	6. **The approval hash must cover changed values**, not only resource names, or an approval for
247	   247	   one IAM policy would let a different change to the same policy through; and it must leave out
248	   248	   values that change on every build, or an approval never matches. ⚠️ From memory, not checked:
249	   249	   Serverless puts a timestamped path in the Lambda `Code.S3Key` and a code hash in
250	   250	   `AWS::Lambda::Version` logical IDs; both are left out of the hash.
251	   251	7. **Fail-safe CODEOWNERS default** [design]: without it, root `package.json`, a new stack or a new
252	   252	   `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` folder would be unowned, and GitHub then accepts an approval from
253	   253	   any writer (📖 about code owners).
254	   254	8. **Same-repository reusable workflows can use `uses: $/.github/workflows/<file>`**, which GitHub
255	   255	   now recommends: it resolves to the running commit, not to the runner's workspace (📖 GitHub docs
256	   256	   source, `data/reusables/actions/reusable-workflow-calling-syntax.md`; flagged by zizmor's
257	   257	   `self-repository` audit). `actionlint` 1.7.12 (✅ latest release on 2026-11-09, published
258	   258	   2026-03-30) does not know the syntax; `validate.sh` ignores only that message.
259	   259	9. **`runner.temp` is not available in job-level `env`** (✅ caught by `actionlint`); paths use
260	   260	   `$RUNNER_TEMP` inside steps.

263	   263	
264	   264	10. **SCP "protect the org trail" is mostly redundant** for member accounts: they cannot delete
265	   265	    an organization trail or turn its logging off anyway (📖 R2.6.2). E5 instead denies changes
266	   266	    to any trail inside prod accounts. The framework's layer-1 bullet is reworded in the final pass.
267	   267	11. **"Metadata" reads can leak configuration, data or secrets** (⚠️ response contents from
268	   268	    memory of the API references): `lambda:ListFunctions` and `ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition` return
269	   269	    environment variables and cannot be limited to one resource (✅ catalogue: not resource-scoped);
270	   270	    `lambda:GetFunction` also returns a code download URL; `ecs:DescribeTasks` returns container
271	   271	    environment overrides; `cloudformation:DescribeStacks` returns stack outputs (it could be scoped
272	   272	    per stack); `cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents` returns `ResourceProperties`, "the properties
273	   273	    used to create the resource" (📖 [StackEvent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/APIReference/API_StackEvent.html)),
274	   274	    which for a function includes its environment variables (⚠️ inferred); `logs:DescribeQueries`
275	   275	    returns other users' query strings. E6 leaves all of them out [design];
276	   276	    `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` is granted per function instead.
277	   277	12. **AWS's annotations are signals, not a classification of customer data**: `IsDataPlane` marks
278	   278	    `cloudwatch:GetMetricData` too; `sqs:ListQueues` is not marked `IsList`; and many `IsList`
279	   279	    actions return data or configuration (`s3:ListBucket` object keys, `ec2:Describe*` launch
280	   280	    templates, `ssm:ListCommandInvocations` output; ✅ annotations in the catalogue, ⚠️ response
281	   281	    contents from memory). The tests use an explicit allowlist for `Resource: "*"`. One entry has a
282	   282	    condition: `states:ListExecutions` returns execution names, so names must not be built from
283	   283	    claim data [design].
284	   284	13. **Two prod deploy roles** (framework layer 1 already implies it): the SCP exempts the Pulumi
285	   285	    role from the Lambda-update deny, but not the Serverless role, so `serverless deploy function`
286	   286	    cannot change a function outside CloudFormation (drift). It does not stop malicious code in
287	   287	    the job (Limits). `deploy-prod.yml` has one credentials step per tool, so an unset role
288	   288	    variable fails instead of falling back to the other role.
289	   289	14. **The claim-data deny assumes a naming convention** [design]: every legitimate reader must
290	   290	    match `app-claims-*` or a `DataRead-*` permission set. Lambda execution roles behind SQS event
291	   291	    sources, Step Functions execution roles and an AWS Backup role that reads the bucket would be
292	   292	    denied otherwise (only service-linked roles are outside SCPs, 📖 R2.3.2). Phase-2 prerequisite:
293	   293	    inventory the real callers of these actions (CloudTrail, IAM last-accessed data) and add them
294	   294	    before the SCP is attached.
295	   295	15. **The trail deny blocks every principal in prod accounts**, including deploy roles and
296	   296	    `OrganizationAccountAccessRole`: a member-account trail can only be changed after a temporary
297	   297	    change to the SCP (an L3 path), or an exempt audit role would have to be added [design].
298	   298	16. **Exempt role names must be protected** (OD19): the exemptions are name patterns, so anyone in
299	   299	    a prod account who could create or re-trust a role named `app-claims-*` or `cfn-deployment-*`
300	   300	    would bypass both denies. E5 lets only `github-prod-deploy-pulumi` change those roles.
301	   301	    - **Today that role deploys every Pulumi stack**, not only the IAM stack, and any job in the
302	   302	      deploy workflow can obtain it (OD20). So "only the IAM stack" holds only after OD20 (since
303	   303	      OD22: phase 1, E4, E4b) gives the
304	   304	      IAM stack its own role and OIDC subject; until then the protection is "only an approved prod
305	   305	      Pulumi deploy" (agent's reading of OD19, confirmed by the owner 2026-11-09).
306	   306	    - **Residual risks:** a principal that may pass an `app-claims-*` role could create a new
307	   307	      function with it (`lambda:CreateFunction` is not denied), and one that may pass
308	   308	      `cfn-deployment-*` to CloudFormation could change any function through a template;
309	   309	      `iam:PassRole` is left out on purpose because the Serverless role must pass
310	   310	      `cfn-deployment-*`. An `InfraOperator-*` grant may change an `app-claims` function's code
311	   311	      and so read claim data indirectly (accepted with break-glass, ADR-0005; JIT reconciliation
312	   312	      in layer 7 is the control).
313	   313	    - **Constraints and prerequisites (phase 2):** Serverless services cannot create their own
314	   314	      `app-claims-*` execution roles (CloudFormation runs as `cfn-deployment-*`, not exempt); those
315	   315	      roles live in the Pulumi IAM stack and are referenced by ARN. The protected roles must exist
316	   316	      before the SCP is attached, and if `github-prod-deploy-pulumi`'s own trust breaks (e.g. the
317	   317	      subject-format opt-in of E4), only an SCP change from the management account (an L3 path)
318	   318	      can repair it.
319	   319	17. **Gaps in the claim-data deny, under G13** (⚠️ not verified): S3 requests through access
320	   320	    points may be authorised on the access-point ARN, not the bucket ARN; KMS `Decrypt` on the
321	   321	    claim keys would be a second layer.
322	   322	    The deny also covers `sqs:StartMessageMoveTask` (a write, ✅ catalogue), which could move claim
323	   323	    messages to another queue; cost: a JIT grant cannot redrive a claims dead-letter queue.
324	   324	
325	   325	### Step 3 (agent runtime, supply chain, policy pack)
326	   326	
327	   327	18. **The settings schema on schemastore.org is community-maintained and lags behind**: it accepts
328	   328	    unknown keys and lacks `allowedProviders` and `managedSourcesBehavior` (✅ checked). The tests
329	   329	    therefore check keys by path and require a documentation source for every key it lacks.
330	   330	19. **The phase-1 allowlist gives no protection for `~/.aws`, and a "read-only" wildcard rule
331	   331	    can write files** (review step 3): Claude Code runs a built-in set of read-only commands
332	   332	    (`cat`, `grep`, `head`, read-only `git` …) without a prompt in every mode, and the set is not
333	   333	    configurable (📖 [permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md#read-only-commands)).
334	   334	    Leaving `cat` out of the allowlist protected nothing. Worse, `Bash(git log *)`, `Bash(git show *)`
335	   335	    and `Bash(git diff *)` also match `--output=<path>`, which writes chosen content to any path
336	   336	    (✅ git 2.34.1; the docs use `git log --output=<file>` as an example match). The allowlist is now
337	   337	    two exact repo scripts, and those run whatever `package.json` says [limit]. Owner decision OD21
338	   338	    adds two keys to phase 1: a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule, which also applies to recognized
339	   339	    `cat`/`head`/`tail` (📖 permissions), and `autoMode.classifyAllShell` (📖, ≥ 2.1.193), so the two
340	   340	    allow rules do not skip the auto-mode classifier. Left open until the phase-2 sandbox: a command
341	   341	    that reads files without naming them (`grep -r` from `~`) or a script that opens `~/.aws` itself
342	   342	    is not covered by a deny rule (📖 permissions). Not chosen: `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`
343	   343	    (📖, ≥ 2.1.257), which would also block every read outside the repository.
344	   344	20. **Credential paths beyond the HIPAA template** [design]: `~/.aws` as a whole (the SSO token
345	   345	    cache opens every role of the engineer, layer 2), `~/.kube`, `~/.pulumi`, `~/.config/gcloud`,
346	   346	    the Firebase CLI token, `~/.docker/config.json`. `~/.config/gh` must be hidden from the sandbox
347	   347	    too, not only from Claude's Read tool: sandboxed commands run without a prompt (OD12) and
348	   348	    `api.github.com` is allowed, so a readable token lets the agent approve PRs as the engineer (OD5).
349	   349	    This closes only the sandboxed route: an excluded CLI (`pulumi`, `serverless`) runs repository
350	   350	    code outside the sandbox with full access (finding 22), so hiding credentials from the sandbox
351	   351	    is hygiene, not a boundary (ADR-0007).
352	   352	21. **TypeScript 7 is not yet supported by `@pulumi/pulumi`** (✅ npm peer-dependency error:
353	   353	    `typescript >= 3.8.3 < 7`); the pack pins TypeScript 6.0.3.
354	   354	22. **`sandbox.excludedCommands` entries match like `Bash(...)` rules** (📖
355	   355	    [sandboxing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md#run-commands-outside-the-sandbox-with-excludedcommands)):
356	   356	    `aws` alone matches only `aws` with no arguments, so the first draft kept every `aws` call in the
357	   357	    sandbox, where it fails (no `~/.aws`, no AWS endpoints). Entries are now `aws *`, `pulumi *`,
358	   358	    `serverless *`. The docs also answer the framework's ⚠️ on matching: every command in the call
359	   359	    must match; a call with `cd`, a redirect, `$(...)` or a subshell stays sandboxed; the match is on
360	   360	    the text, so `/usr/local/bin/aws`, a script that calls `aws`, and `npx serverless` do not match.
361	   361	    Excluded commands go through the permission flow: they prompt in Manual mode, but in auto mode
362	   362	    the classifier decides (📖 sandboxing), so phase 2 also lists them as `ask` rules, which prompt
363	   363	    in every mode (📖 auto-mode-config). The prompt shows the command (`pulumi preview`), not the
364	   364	    repository code it runs, which a sandboxed command may have changed without a prompt.
365	   365	23. **A mandatory Pulumi policy is only advisory while a value is unknown** (✅ `@pulumi/policy`
366	   366	    1.21.0 `server.js` catches `UnknownValueError` and reports `advisory`). A PR-time or prod
367	   367	    preview of a policy built from a resource of the same update passes; the stop comes during the
368	   368	    update. Access Analyzer is the preview-time check (layer 5).
369	   369	24. **The first policy pack missed the usual ways to grant admin** (review step 3): user and
370	   370	    group policies, `AdministratorAccess` attached by ARN, `Role.managedPolicyArns`, and wildcards
371	   371	    such as `iam:Pass*`. All are now covered and tested. Round 2: IAM also accepts `?`, so `s3:?*` and
372	   372	    `*?` are full wildcards (📖 IAM Action element); covered too. Round 3: a wildcard in the service
373	   373	    prefix (`*:*`, `s?:Get*`) is refused as a full wildcard (⚠️ whether IAM accepts it is unverified).

375	   375	    auto-mode-config: a list without `"$defaults"` replaces the built-in rules; entries from managed

1	# Reusable production deploy (framework layer 3 "Merge approval = deploy approval", layer 5).
     2	# The ONLY workflow that references the `production` environment. Called by deploy-on-main.yml.
     3	#
     4	# Conditions this file must keep (checked by examples/tests/test_workflow_policy.py):
     5	# - no ref/SHA input: it deploys the commit that was merged (github.sha of the push to main);
     6	# - one concurrency group per stack without cancel-in-progress, so a running deploy is never
     7	#   cancelled (Pulumi guide: that can leave infrastructure half-applied). GitHub still cancels
     8	#   a run that is only *pending* when a newer one arrives, so not every merged commit gets its
     9	#   own deploy run; the newer run deploys both commits;
    10	# - OIDC only (id-token: write); no AWS keys; every action pinned to a full commit SHA;
    11	# - it deploys only the current tip of main: re-running an old run (allowed for writers for 30
    12	#   days, same GITHUB_SHA) would otherwise roll prod back without any approval;
    13	# - prod preview -> risk stop -> apply; the risk stop step cannot be skipped or ignored.
    14	#   No --skip-preview/-f, --target/-t, --exclude, --replace, state, import, destroy.
    15	# - one GitHub environment per kind of stack (OD22): the IAM stack deploys from
    16	#   `production-iam`, every other stack from `production`. Each environment has its own OIDC
    17	#   subject, so its own deploy roles (examples/aws/): code running in a domain stack's job
    18	#   cannot obtain the IAM stack's role, the only role that may change SCP-exempt roles.
    19	# - no install scripts run (npm_config_ignore_scripts), except for the packages on the reviewed
    20	#   allowlist tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt, an L3 path (OD22).
    21	#
    22	# Known limits (examples/README.md): the stack's own code (the Pulumi program, Serverless
    23	# plugins) runs with that stack's deploy role during preview and apply, so the risk stop
    24	# catches risky diffs nobody looked at, not malicious code that was approved; OD22 limits the
    25	# damage to what that stack's role may do. `pulumi up` previews again; a change made outside
    26	# the pipeline between the two previews is not re-checked.
    27	#
    28	# Variables of both environments (not secrets; same names, values per environment): AWS_REGION,
    29	# PROD_PULUMI_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, PROD_SERVERLESS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, PULUMI_BACKEND_URL,
    30	# PULUMI_CLI_VERSION, NODE_VERSION. The Serverless License Key is read from
    31	# SSM Parameter Store with the deploy role (sf >= 4.4.19, R4.4.8), so no CI secret holds it.
    32	name: deploy-prod
    33	
    34	on:
    35	  workflow_call:
    36	    inputs:
    37	      stack:
    38	        description: Stack name, e.g. claims-data. Also the deploy-approvals/<stack>/ directory.
    39	        type: string
    40	        required: true
    41	      tool:
    42	        description: "pulumi, serverless or sql (database changes, ADR-0011)"
    43	        type: string
    44	        required: true
    45	      workdir:
    46	        description: Directory of the stack in the monorepo
    47	        type: string
    48	        required: true
    49	
    50	permissions: {}
    51	
    52	jobs:
    53	  deploy:
    54	    name: deploy ${{ inputs.stack }} to production
    55	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    56	    # OD22: only the IAM stack gets `production-iam` (and so the IAM deploy role). The mapping
    57	    # lives here, in an L3 path, not in a caller input. `inputs` is available in `environment`
    58	    # (✅ actionlint 1.7.12, which checks context availability, accepts it).
    59	    environment: ${{ inputs.stack == 'iam' && 'production-iam' || 'production' }}
    60	    permissions:
    61	      contents: read   # check out the merged commit
    62	      id-token: write  # OIDC to the prod deploy role; no stored AWS keys
    63	    concurrency:
    64	      group: deploy-prod-${{ inputs.stack }}
    65	      cancel-in-progress: false
    66	    env:
    67	      STACK: ${{ inputs.stack }}
    68	      TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
    69	      WORKDIR: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
    70	      # Every npm, npx and `pulumi install` in this job skips lifecycle scripts (R9.1.13: "npm
    71	      # does not run scripts specified in package.json files"; ⚠️ whether this covers every
    72	      # dependency's scripts is not stated, test on the runner).
    73	      npm_config_ignore_scripts: "true"
    74	    steps:
    75	      - name: Check out the merged commit, with history for the risk-stop approval checks
    76	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
    77	        with:
    78	          persist-credentials: false
    79	          fetch-depth: 0
    80	
    81	      - name: Set up Node.js
    82	        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
    83	        with:
    84	          node-version: ${{ vars.NODE_VERSION }}
    85	
    86	      - name: Refuse to deploy anything but the current tip of main
    87	        env:
    88	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    89	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    90	        run: |
    91	          # git/ref/heads/main names the branch explicitly; a tag called `main` cannot match.
    92	          tip=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/git/ref/heads/main" --jq .object.sha)
    93	          if [ "$tip" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
    94	            echo "This run is for $GITHUB_SHA but main is at $tip (re-run, or a newer merge)."
    95	            echo "Nothing is deployed; the run for the newer commit deploys both."
    96	            echo "If no newer run exists (e.g. its message had [skip ci]), merge an empty change."
    97	            exit 1
    98	          fi
    99	
   100	      # Everything that downloads code is installed here, before the AWS credentials are in the
   101	      # job's environment, and with install scripts off (job env above). A script that does run
   102	      # (allowlist below) can still request the job's OIDC token, since id-token: write is
   103	      # job-wide, or leave a process behind (examples/README.md, "Limits").
   104	      - name: Install dependencies before any prod credential exists in the job
   105	        if: inputs.tool != 'sql'
   106	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   107	        run: npm ci
   108	
   109	      # `npm rebuild <pkg>` runs the install scripts of the named packages only (R9.1.13).
   110	      # The list is reviewed by the L3 owner team (CODEOWNERS: /tools/ci/).
   111	      - name: Run install scripts of allowlisted packages only
   112	        if: inputs.tool != 'sql'
   113	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   114	        run: |
   115	          mapfile -t allowed < <(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt")
   116	          if [ "${#allowed[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   117	            npm rebuild --ignore-scripts=false "${allowed[@]}"
   118	          fi
   119	
   120	      - name: Install the Pulumi CLI only
   121	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   122	        uses: pulumi/actions@8e5e406f4007fca908480587cb9893c07090f58d # v7.0.0
   123	        with:
   124	          pulumi-version: ${{ vars.PULUMI_CLI_VERSION }}
   125	
   126	      - name: Install Pulumi plugins and the policy pack before credentials
   127	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   128	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   129	        run: |
   130	          pulumi install
   131	          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/policy-packs/aws"
   132	          npm ci
   133	          pulumi install
   134	
   135	      # ⚠️ From memory, not verified: Serverless v4's npm package downloads the framework on
   136	      # first run. Running it once here keeps that download before the credentials. Whether
   137	      # `--version` works before authentication (R4.4.8) is also unverified.
   138	      - name: Install the Serverless Framework before credentials
   139	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   140	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   141	        run: npx serverless --version
   142	
   143	      # Two roles per environment (framework layer 1; SCP in examples/aws/scp-prod-ou.json): only
   144	      # the Pulumi role is exempt from the Lambda-update deny; the Serverless role only passes the
   145	      # CloudFormation deploymentRole. This stops drift from `serverless deploy function`. Code in
   146	      # this job can still request an OIDC token for either role of ITS environment, not for the
   147	      # other environment's roles (OD22; examples/README.md, "Limits"). One step per tool, so an
   148	      # unset variable fails the step instead of falling back to the other role.
   149	      - name: AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC (Pulumi deploy role)
   150	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   151	        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
   152	        with:
   153	          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.PROD_PULUMI_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
   154	          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
   155	          # The run ID in the session name links CloudTrail events to this run (layer 7 change record).
   156	          role-session-name: deploy-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
   157	
   158	      - name: AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC (Serverless deploy role)
   159	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   160	        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
   161	        with:
   162	          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.PROD_SERVERLESS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
   163	          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
   164	          role-session-name: deploy-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
   165	
   166	      # Database changes (layer 3 "Database changes", ADR-0011, OD29). The role may only
   167	      # `rds-db:connect` as the migration database user (IAM database authentication, R9.2.11);
   168	      # no person holds database credentials.
   169	      - name: AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC (database change role)
   170	        if: inputs.tool == 'sql'
   171	        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
   172	        with:
   173	          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.PROD_DB_CHANGE_ROLE_ARN }}
   174	          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
   175	          role-session-name: deploy-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
   176	
   177	      - name: Preview prod (Pulumi)
   178	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   179	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   180	        env:
   181	          PULUMI_BACKEND_URL: ${{ vars.PULUMI_BACKEND_URL }}
   182	        run: pulumi preview --stack "$STACK" --json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"
   183	
   184	      # Serverless Framework v4 (sf-core >= 4.37.0 for `diff`)
   185	      - name: Package once and diff against prod (Serverless)
   186	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   187	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   188	        run: |
   189	          npx serverless package --stage prod --package "$RUNNER_TEMP/sls-package"
   190	          npx serverless diff --stage prod --package "$RUNNER_TEMP/sls-package" --json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"
   191	
   192	      # [design] The two tools/db scripts wrap Papaya's migration tool, which is not known here
   193	      # (an L3 path, like the risk stop). pending.sh writes the migration and data-fix files not
   194	      # yet applied as {"files": [{"path", "kind", "sql"}]}; apply.sh applies exactly the files
   195	      # in that JSON, in order, each in its own transaction, and rolls a data fix back when its
   196	      # affected-row count differs from its `-- expected_rows: N` header.
   197	      - name: List pending SQL files (database)
   198	        if: inputs.tool == 'sql'
   199	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   200	        run: '"$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/tools/db/pending.sh" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"'
   201	
   202	      # Risk stop (layer 3). Exit 0: no risky change, or a valid approval matches this preview.
   203	      # Exit 3: risky change without a valid approval. Exit 2: unreadable preview. Any non-zero
   204	      # exit fails the job here, before any Apply step. The summary goes to the job summary and
   205	      # lists resource type, name, operation and changed property names, never values.
   206	      - name: Risk stop
   207	        run: >-
   208	          python3 tools/risk-stop/classify.py
   209	          --tool "$TOOL" --preview "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"
   210	          --approvals "deploy-approvals/$STACK" --repo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --workdir "$WORKDIR"
   211	          --summary "$RUNNER_TEMP/risk-summary.md"
   212	
   213	      - name: Keep the filtered preview summary as evidence
   214	        if: always()
   215	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
   216	        with:
   217	          name: risk-summary-${{ inputs.stack }}
   218	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/risk-summary.md
   219	          if-no-files-found: ignore
   220	
   221	      # --yes is needed in CI (no terminal). Pulumi previews again before applying; a mandatory
   222	      # policy violation stops the update (R4.2.2). This is the phase-2 shape: until the policy
   223	      # pack exists (phase 2, layer 5), drop --policy-pack here and its install step above.
   224	      - name: Apply (Pulumi)
   225	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   226	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   227	        env:
   228	          PULUMI_BACKEND_URL: ${{ vars.PULUMI_BACKEND_URL }}
   229	        run: pulumi up --stack "$STACK" --yes --policy-pack "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/policy-packs/aws"
   230	
   231	      - name: Apply (database), the files that were classified
   232	        if: inputs.tool == 'sql'
   233	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   234	        run: '"$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/tools/db/apply.sh" "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"'
   235	
   236	      - name: Apply (Serverless), deploying the package that was diffed
   237	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   238	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   239	        run: npx serverless deploy --stage prod --package "$RUNNER_TEMP/sls-package"

     2	# Lives at .github/CODEOWNERS on the base branch. Team names and the directory layout are
     3	# illustrative placeholders: Papaya's real layout is not known.
     4	#
     5	# Teams (all need explicit write access, or GitHub silently assigns no owner):
     6	#   @example-org/l3-owners         L3 owner team: process-defining paths and the SCP stack (OD13)
     7	#   @example-org/oncall-approvers  on-call approver group: co-owns every deployable path (OD9)
     8	#   @example-org/team-claims, @example-org/team-underwriting, @example-org/team-web
     9	#                                  domain teams
    10	#   @example-org/data-owners-tenant-a  data owners of one insurer tenant (layer 6, OD29)
    11	#
    12	# ORDER MATTERS: the last matching pattern wins (GitHub docs, about-code-owners).

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Decision logic of the `approval-gate` required check (framework layer 3; gap G19) [design].
     3	
     4	The GitHub App that runs this (hosting, key storage, triggers: still open, G19) collects the
     5	input below from GitHub (PR, reviews, CODEOWNERS owners per file, team members), from the
     6	incident register and from the on-call schedule, and posts the result as the `approval-gate`
     7	check, which the ruleset requires (E1). This file is the part that can be written and tested
     8	without a live system.
     9	
    10	  exit 0  pass: every rule holds
    11	  exit 1  fail: the check stays red, merge is blocked
    12	  exit 2  input cannot be read: fail closed
    13	
    14	Rules:
    15	  R1  An approval counts only if it is an APPROVED review on the PR's head commit, by a human,
    16	      who is not the author, not the last pusher and not the person who triggered an
    17	      app-opened PR (layer 5; OD5). Reviews carry `commit_id`, `submitted_at`, `user` (📖 R9.1.10).
    18	  R2  Every changed file needs a counted approval from a member of one of its owner teams.
    19	      An approval from the on-call group counts for a file of another team only if the PR
    20	      carries the `incident` label, links an incident that is open now, and the approver is on
    21	      shift now (OD27). Anyone with Triage can apply a label (📖 R9.1.9), so the label alone
    22	      grants nothing.
    23	  R3  A file owned only by the L3 owner team (a process path: workflows, CODEOWNERS, agent
    24	      config, catalogue, SCP stack, risk stop, ...) needs counted approvals from TWO different
    25	      L3 owner team members (OD26). The ruleset keeps one approval for the rest of the repository,
    26	      because a path-scoped reviewer rule was not found for GitHub Team (📖 R9.1.15).
    27	  R4  A file whose owners include a tenant's data-owner team (`data-owners-<tenant>`: a data fix,
    28	      L3-data-write, OD29) needs, besides the R2 approval, an approval from a member of that team
    29	      who is a different person. In an incident the on-call approver stands in for the data owner,
    30	      who reviews it the next working day (layer 6); the check passes with a warning.
    31	  W1  Warning, not a failure: an approval submitted less than MIN_REVIEW_SECONDS after the last
    32	      push, or between 22:00 and 06:00 in the approver's own time zone without an open incident. Warnings go to the
    33	      monthly report (layer 7) as signals of rubber-stamping or of an approval made through a
    34	      compromised login (threat T23). Nothing here can tell a web approval from an API one
    35	      (📖 R9.1.10).
    36	
    37	Input JSON:
    38	  {"pr": {"author": "a", "last_pusher": "a", "triggered_by": null, "head_sha": "<sha>",
    39	          "last_push_at": "...", "labels": ["incident"], "incident_id": "INC-12",
    40	          "files": {"services/claims/serverless.yml": ["team-claims", "oncall-approvers"]}},
    41	   "reviews": [{"user": "b", "user_type": "User", "state": "APPROVED", "commit_id": "<sha>",
    42	                "submitted_at": "..."}],
    43	   "teams": {"team-claims": ["a", "c"], "oncall-approvers": ["b"], "l3-owners": ["d", "e"]},
    44	   "open_incidents": ["INC-12"], "on_shift": ["b"], "utc_offsets": {"b": 8}}
    45	  `open_incidents` and `on_shift` are read by the app when the check runs: in phase 1 from the
    46	  incident issues in Linear and the schedule file `oncall/schedule.yaml` (an L3 path); from
    47	  phase 2 from the paging tool (G5).
    48	"""
    49	import datetime
    50	import json
    51	import sys
    52	
    53	ONCALL = "oncall-approvers"
    54	L3 = "l3-owners"
    55	DATA_OWNERS = "data-owners-"
    56	MIN_REVIEW_SECONDS = 120  # [design] calibrate from the first months of data
    57	NIGHT_START, NIGHT_END = 22, 6  # local hours, [design]
    58	DEFAULT_UTC_OFFSET = 7  # Vietnam, Thailand; Hong Kong is +8, so offsets come per approver
    59	
    60	
    61	def _time(s):
    62	    return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    63	
    64	
    65	def counted_approvals(data):
    66	    """R1: the approvals that count, latest per user."""
    67	    pr = data["pr"]
    68	    excluded = {pr["author"], pr["last_pusher"], pr.get("triggered_by")}
    69	    latest = {}
    70	    for r in sorted(data["reviews"], key=lambda r: r["submitted_at"]):
    71	        latest[r["user"]] = r  # a later review (e.g. changes requested) replaces an earlier one
    72	    return [r for r in latest.values()
    73	            if r["state"] == "APPROVED" and r["commit_id"] == pr["head_sha"]
    74	            and r.get("user_type", "User") == "User" and r["user"] not in excluded]
    75	
    76	
    77	def incident_active(data):
    78	    pr = data["pr"]
    79	    return "incident" in pr.get("labels", []) and pr.get("incident_id") in data.get("open_incidents", [])
    80	
    81	
    82	def decide(data):
    83	    """Return (passed, reasons, warnings)."""
    84	    teams, pr = data["teams"], data["pr"]
    85	    approvals = counted_approvals(data)
    86	    approvers = {r["user"] for r in approvals}
    87	    on_shift = set(data.get("on_shift", []))
    88	    incident = incident_active(data)
    89	    reasons, warnings = [], []
    90	
    91	    for path, owners in sorted(pr["files"].items()):
    92	        if owners == [L3]:  # R3: process path
    93	            l3 = approvers & set(teams.get(L3, []))
    94	            if len(l3) < 2:
    95	                reasons.append(f"{path}: process path, needs 2 approvals from {L3} (has {len(l3)})")
    96	            continue
    97	        data_teams = [t for t in owners if t.startswith(DATA_OWNERS)]
    98	        code_owners = [t for t in owners if t not in data_teams]
    99	        r2_users, oncall_users = set(), set()
   100	        for user in approvers:  # R2
   101	            domain = any(user in teams.get(t, []) for t in code_owners if t != ONCALL)
   102	            oncall = ONCALL in code_owners and user in teams.get(ONCALL, []) and incident and user in on_shift
   103	            if domain or oncall:
   104	                r2_users.add(user)
   105	            if oncall:
   106	                oncall_users.add(user)
   107	        if not r2_users:
   108	            hint = "" if incident else " (on-call approvals count only with an open incident and on shift)"
   109	            reasons.append(f"{path}: no counted approval from {', '.join(code_owners)}{hint}")
   110	        elif data_teams:  # R4
   111	            data_users = {u for u in approvers for t in data_teams if u in teams.get(t, [])}
   112	            if any(d != u for d in data_users for u in r2_users):
   113	                pass
   114	            elif oncall_users:
   115	                warnings.append(f"{path}: data owner stood in for by the on-call approver; review due next working day")
   116	            else:
   117	                reasons.append(f"{path}: data fix needs a second approval from {', '.join(data_teams)}")
   118	
   119	    last_push = _time(pr["last_push_at"])
   120	    for r in approvals:  # W1
   121	        t = _time(r["submitted_at"])
   122	        if (t - last_push).total_seconds() < MIN_REVIEW_SECONDS:
   123	            warnings.append(f"{r['user']}: approved {int((t - last_push).total_seconds())} s after the last push")
   124	        offset = data.get("utc_offsets", {}).get(r["user"], DEFAULT_UTC_OFFSET)
   125	        local_hour = (t.hour + offset) % 24
   126	        if (local_hour >= NIGHT_START or local_hour < NIGHT_END) and not incident:
   127	            warnings.append(f"{r['user']}: approved at night without an open incident")
   128	    if not approvals:
   129	        reasons.append("no counted approval")
   130	    return not reasons, reasons, warnings
   131	
   132	
   133	def main(argv=None):
   134	    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
   135	    try:
   136	        with open(argv[0]) as f:
   137	            data = json.load(f)
   138	        passed, reasons, warnings = decide(data)
   139	    except Exception as e:  # fail closed
   140	        print(f"approval-gate: cannot read input ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); failing", file=sys.stderr)
   141	        return 2
   142	    for line in reasons:
   143	        print("FAIL", line)
   144	    for line in warnings:
   145	        print("WARN", line)
   146	    print("approval-gate:", "pass" if passed else "fail")
   147	    return 0 if passed else 1
   148	
   149	
   150	if __name__ == "__main__":
   151	    sys.exit(main())

{
  "deployment_branch_policy": {
    "protected_branches": false,
    "custom_branch_policies": true
  }
}
# PR preview against NON-PROD only (framework layer 3, "Pulumi" bullet): a prod preview would run
# the PR's code with prod state-write and secret access. Prod is previewed only on main, in
# deploy-prod.yml, after the merge.
# The non-prod role trusts the `pull_request` subject of this repository; it has no prod access.
name: pr-preview-nonprod

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  preview:
    name: preview ${{ matrix.stack }} (non-prod)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read   # check out the PR
      id-token: write  # OIDC to the non-prod preview role
    concurrency:
      group: pr-preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-${{ matrix.stack }}
      cancel-in-progress: true  # previews only; nothing is applied
    env:
      npm_config_ignore_scripts: "true"  # PR code's install scripts never run (OD22)
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - stack: claims-data

      - name: Check out the PR
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

input.message:
## Grading report: Papaya DevSecOps Challenge 1 submission

I only read files. Nothing was edited. One local check: I ran `python3 -m unittest discover -p 'test_*.py'` in `examples/tests` with TMPDIR set to the scratchpad and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. Result: **157 tests, OK** (✅). `examples/README.md` still reports "Ran 108 tests".

### Verdicts

**1. Does it answer the question?**
Mostly yes. It answers how Papaya should **control** coding agents. It does not say much about how Papaya should **use** them.
- **Strengths:**
  - It takes a clear position on the Engineering vs Compliance conflict: Compliance's sentence only covers prod writes.
  - The workflow is concrete: L0–L3 risk levels, merge-to-`main` as the gate, a risk stop, an incident lane with a 2 a.m. example, and a JIT fallback.
  - The rest of the package is real: an engineer guide, a rollout plan, a control register, a threat model, ADRs and tested example files.
- **Weaknesses:**
  - The agent appears almost only as a risk to contain. Productive DevSecOps uses get little design: security review, CVE/dependency fixes, alert triage, evidence generation, shared skills.
  - The package is about 39k words. The framework alone has 161 OD-codes and 307 R-codes. The decision panel cannot read it in the "~15 min" the README promises.

**2. Where is it generic boilerplate?**
- Layer 5 CI hardening: OIDC, restricted `GITHUB_TOKEN`, SHA pinning, no `pull_request_target`, SAST and secret scan as required checks.
- Layer 7: org CloudTrail to a log-archive account, drift detection, break-glass principles.
- Layer 8 governance ("every control has an owner, a metric and a review date").
- The MCP review checklist.
- Threats T11, T13, T15 and T16.
- The ISO/HIPAA crosswalk. Its ISO IDs are marked "recalled, not read".
- The phase-2 managed settings are explicitly Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, with "every key kept as written except" a deviation list.

All of this is correct, and it is labelled with Papaya names. But it would read the same at any AWS + GitHub company.

**3. Where does it show Papaya-specific thinking?**
This is the strongest part of the submission:
- **Serverless:** the SCP that denies Lambda updates exempts CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s but not the Serverless deploy role. This closes `serverless deploy function` drift.
- **Pulumi:** PR previews run on non-prod only, because a prod preview needs state-write access.
- **GitHub Team limits:** there are no environment reviewers, so the design adds a risk stop with a preview-hash approval PR. This is implemented and tested in E7.
- **Monorepo CODEOWNERS:** on-call co-ownership, limited by an approval-gate app (E12).
- **Tenant data:** data fixes per insurer tenant with data-owner teams. Hasura metadata is treated as tenant isolation.
- **Log masking:** CloudWatch custom identifiers for VN/TH/HK, because AWS has none for these countries.
- **Platform facts:** Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list. The k0s audit log depends on `extraArgs`.
- **Approval records:** Linear instead of Slack.
- **Metadata reads:** an honest analysis of "metadata" reads that can leak Serverless plain-text secrets (E6).
- **Regional law:** Vietnam Decree 356 / Law 91.

**4. What is missing compared with the challenge and Appendix A?**
- **Platforms:**
  - GCP (Vertex AI / Gemini, where partner documents are processed): human and agent access is an open gap (G3).
  - k0s (it runs the production AI agents): interim measures only.
  - Firebase: weaker controls.
  - Never mentioned at all: mobile (React Native / Expo builds and OTA updates, a prod change path), EC2, SNS, Next.js hosting, ML model deploys (✅ grep found zero hits).
- **Monitoring:** the brief's "fragmented monitoring" gets one principle and a phase-2 placeholder (G5).
- **Feasibility:** there is no effort estimate for a phase 1 of 23 items for 1–2 people.
- **Risk acceptance:** residual risks are shown as "accepted by the owner". That "owner" is the candidate, not a Papaya risk owner.

### Findings (most severe first)

| # | Severity | Location | Problem | Suggested fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | critical | `README.md:22`; `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:294` (S4 "no new step in the non-prod loop"); `examples/claude/managed-settings.phase2.json` (`ask: Bash(aws *)…`, `sandbox.credentials`); `examples/README.md:132-143`; `examples/claude/marketplace/plugins/devsecops-guardrails/skills/prod-change/SKILL.md` step 2 | The central promise to Engineering is "a free non-prod loop with the agent". The design's own phase-2 settings contradict it. Every `aws`/`pulumi`/`serverless` call prompts, in non-prod and in auto mode too. The sandbox hides git, `gh`, `~/.kube`, `gcloud` and `~/.npmrc` credentials, so the agent can no longer push, open PRs, run Docker or Testcontainers, or install from a private registry. The brief says Claude Code is how engineers run git and open PRs. These costs appear only in the examples README and the guide, not in the README's "Costs" row or in S4. | Either scope the `ask` rules and credential hiding to prod-capable sessions (e.g. a non-prod devcontainer or remote environment where they are relaxed), or restate S4 honestly. Then list "agent cannot push / open PRs; prompt per cloud CLI call" in the README cost row. |
| 2 | major | `docs/01-framework.md` layer 5 "Agent review" / "Agents in CI" (≈674-684); `examples/claude/marketplace/` (the only internal plugin is the `prod-change` guardrail skill); `docs/02-engineer-guide.md` §1 ("use Claude Code as you do today") | The question asks how Papaya **uses** coding agents for DevSecOps. The design specifies almost only restrictions. The CI agent is defined by what it may not do, not by its tasks. There are no designed agent workflows for security review, dependency/CVE fixes, alert triage, runbook execution or evidence collection. There is no shared `CLAUDE.md`/skills content for Pulumi or Serverless conventions. | Add a "how agents are used" layer: 4–6 named agent workflows, each with its session type, identity, plugin/skill and output (PR, report, ticket), and the metric that shows the value. |
| 3 | major | `docs/01-framework.md:462-479`; `docs/adr/0011-database-changes-through-the-pipeline.md` §3; `examples/github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml:55,169-200`; `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:231,246` (hard prerequisite 7) | The `sql` job runs on a GitHub-hosted runner (`ubuntu-24.04`) and connects to Aurora with IAM auth. Nothing says how the runner reaches a normally private, VPC-only Aurora cluster. Layer 5 itself warns against self-hosted runners. Hasura metadata is normally applied through Hasura's metadata API with an admin secret, not through a DB role. Yet the docs state as fact (no marker) that the job's only credential is `rds-db:connect` and that "no person holds database credentials". This path is a hard prerequisite for removing standing prod write. If it is not workable, that promise slips. | Name where SQL runs (e.g. CI starts a one-off ECS task or Lambda inside the VPC with the migration role, or an isolated self-hosted runner, with the G15 risk recorded). Specify how Hasura metadata is applied and where its admin secret lives. Mark the current claim ⚠️. |
| 4 | major | `examples/approval-gate/gate.py:73` (`commit_id == head_sha`); `examples/github/ruleset-main.json:21-22,29` (`require_last_push_approval`, `strict_required_status_checks_policy`); `docs/01-framework.md:382-383` | The branch must be up to date (no merge queue), and the gate counts only approvals on the head commit. So in a shared monorepo, every merge to `main` makes every other ready PR stale: it must be updated and approved again. Process paths need two L3 approvals again. The framework says "whether updating drops approvals is open", but the submission's own E12 makes it certain. This hits S4 and the incident lane, and no cost is stated. | Count an approval while the PR's diff against the merge base is unchanged (e.g. compare a patch-id or tree-diff hash in the gate), or drop the strict up-to-date rule and rely on the post-merge prod preview and risk stop. State the throughput cost. |
| 5 | major | `examples/github/CODEOWNERS:41,50`; `docs/01-framework.md:362` (L3 row "IAM-only stacks are deployable…"), `:81-87`; `docs/adr/0012-approval-integrity-checked-by-the-gate-app.md` §1; `examples/aws/scp-prod-ou.json` (`ExemptRoleNamesOnlyChangedByTheIamStack`) | OD26 requires two approvers on process paths because "one compromised login must not be enough". That covers `.ripgreprc` and `oncall/`. But the IAM stack, the only stack that can create or re-trust the SCP-exempt `app-claims-*` claim-data roles and edit the permissions boundary, needs one approver. That approver is co-owned by on-call and may also approve the same stack's risk-stop PR. This is inconsistent risk calibration. | Treat `infra/pulumi/iam/` as a process path (two L3 members, on-call not a co-owner), or require a second, different approver for `deploy-approvals/iam/`. |
| 6 | major | `docs/01-framework.md:223-228` (GCP: WIF "restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization"); gaps G1–G3 (`:926-928`); `docs/06-problem-control-map.md` A4–A6; Appendix A | Large parts of the stated stack get no workflow. GCP Vertex AI / Gemini, where partner documents are processed, has only CI federation, and only at org level, which is weaker than the AWS environment-scoped trust. k0s is interim only. Firebase has no preview and no leak detection. Mobile (React Native / Expo builds and OTA updates), EC2, SNS and ML model deploys never appear. Each is a prod change path outside "every prod change is a PR". | Add an inventory of prod write paths per platform, with the gate that covers each. Narrow GCP WIF to repository + environment. Cover Expo EAS builds/updates and Vertex model deploys at least at the same pattern level. |
| 7 | major | `docs/01-framework.md:809-814, 848-858`, `:158-160`; `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:221` (1.13); `docs/04-compliance-mapping.md` C-23 | JIT says "on-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant". But the approval is a Linear state change, and the grant tool (partner product / TEAM sample / home-built) is not chosen. Nothing says which component checks approver ≠ requester before `CreateAccountAssignment`, or who performs the grant at 2 a.m. in phase 1. As designed, the rule is detective at best. | Choose the mechanism. Let the grant automation call `CreateAccountAssignment` only after it has checked approver ≠ requester and on-shift from the mirrored issue history. Linear stays the record. |
| 8 | major | `README.md:6,14,69`; `docs/01-framework.md:3,38,55-57`, OD table `:949-992`; every doc's "approved by the owner" status line | Residual risks (JIT meets approval only partly, one approver for L3, admins can edit the gate, k0s/Firebase stored credentials) are shown as already "accepted by the owner". The owner is the candidate, not a Papaya risk owner or Compliance. A Compliance panel would object to risk acceptance by an unnamed non-Papaya party. | Re-label them as "proposed decisions requiring Papaya sign-off (Compliance / CTO)". Give the panel a short list of decisions it must make. |
| 9 | major | `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:205-231, 309-313`; `docs/01-framework.md:92-96` | Phase 1 has 23 items in 30 days for 1–2 DevSecOps people. They include a custom GitHub App that every merge depends on, whose hosting, keys and triggers are not researched (G19); a JIT flow; a Linear webhook mirror; the SQL pipeline; the evidence export; and per-service log masking. Effort is "not estimated". The plan is not credible as written. | Estimate effort. Cut phase 1 to the minimum that safely allows removing standing write. Prefer off-the-shelf parts. Define a degraded mode if the gate app is not ready. |
| 10 | major | `docs/01-framework.md:838-847`; `docs/06-problem-control-map.md:47` (P6a "Partial") | The brief names fragmented monitoring across CloudWatch, GCP and Slack, and informal on-call. The design gives on-call schedules, but alert consolidation is one principle deferred to phase 2 with the tool open (G5).
